message.content:
The number of distinct positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large.  In fact:

| Quantity | Approximate value |
|----------|-------------------|
| **Legal positions** (positions that can actually occur in a real game) | ~ 10⁴³ |
| **All possible positions** (including illegal ones) | ~ 10⁴⁶ |
| **Possible games** (sequences of moves from start to finish) | ~ 10¹²⁰ (the Shannon number) |

So when people talk about “possible arrangements” in chess, they’re usually referring to the ~ 10⁴³ legal positions. This figure comes from combinatorial estimates that take into account the constraints of the game (e.g., piece counts, pawn placement, king safety).
